subject: Request: Exec approval for tailored renewal package (SLA credit + tiered discount)
messages:
From: Sara Bloom <sara@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Renewal discussion + open items

Hi Monica,

We're coming up on our renewal and procurement has asked for a consolidated offer they can take to finance. We're generally happy with Redwood but two things are blocking sign: (1) a competitive list price on year-1, and (2) an operational credit for the Q2 downtime we experienced.

Can you share what flexibility you have on a one-year renewal (we'd prefer to stay on annual), and whether there is a pathway for an uptime credit to address the Q2 incident?

I've copied procurement (procurement@greenlinehealth.com).

Thanks,
Sara Bloom
Director of Platform Ops
Greenline Health

[Attachment: uptime-incident-summary-Q2.xlsx]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bloom <sara@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + open items

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the incident summary. I pulled together a specific proposal that balances our pricing guardrails with the retention needs you've described. Key points: 

- Proposal: 12-month renewal, annual billing.
- Year‑1 list discount: 20% (with a step-down to 10% in year‑2 on a 24-month extension option).
- One-time operational credit: $45,000 applied to the first invoice to address Q2 downtime (this is in lieu of a service credit schedule).
- SLA: proactive SLA uplift to 99.995% monitoring for the renewal term and an SLA playbook commitment (incident reviews within 48 hours).

I've attached the draft proposal PDF. This package is out of our standard T&Cs a bit because of the credit + SLA uplift; I'm going to ask Sean and our finance/leadership for exec approval to finalize. If you have any alternate mixes (e.g., higher discount, lower credit) I can surface that as well.

Next steps: if that package looks reasonable to Greenline, let me know and I will escalate for exec signoff today.

Best,
Monica
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: GHL_MSP_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion + proposed package — request for exec approval

Sean/Laura/Vivek — forwarding Greenline's note and the package I'm proposing (summary below). Need a quick yes/no or suggested edits before I send a formal offer. Timing is tight; procurement wants a final by EOD tomorrow to hit their board cadence.

Deal summary (DL-4721, Greenline Health)
- ARR at renew: $1.2M
- Proposed Year‑1 discount: 20% on existing SKU mix (marginal discounting across token tiers)
- One-time operational credit: $45k to address Q2 downtime
- SLA uplift: 99.995% + committed incident P1 review cadence
- Requested term: 12 months, annual invoice

Why I'm asking for this package:
- Risk of competitive RFP if we don't move (Greenline signaled strong price sensitivity).
- They were long-time customers and the Q2 incident lowered goodwill — the one-time credit acknowledges that.
- This package preserves net retention and puts us in place for expansion in H1.

Ask:
- Exec approval to offer the package as-is, OR a quick alternative we can put forward (e.g., 15% + $60k credit) if you prefer to trade more credit for less discount.

I've attached the proposal and the incident summary. Happy to jump on 15 min if helpful.

Thanks,
Monica

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion + proposed package — request for exec approval

Monica — I reviewed the numbers. Approve the SLA uplift and the $45k credit. I want to protect margin so prefer lowering the discount to 15% year‑1, with a 12‑month commitment. If Greenline pushes back hard on year‑1, be prepared to offer the 20% but require a 24‑month extension and an accelerator on usage-based pricing year‑2.

Please proceed to seek Vivek's signoff on final authority for the discount.

- Laura
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion + proposed package — request for exec approval

Thanks for the context. I approve the following final authorization for DL-4721: 

- Year‑1 discount: 18% (final) on the current SKU mix (we keep control on add-on pricing).
- One-time operational credit: $45,000 (applied to invoice 1).
- SLA uplift: 99.995% as a term attachment; include an SLA playbook and quarterly review for the first year.
- Contract term: 12 months, annual billing. If they want 24 months to get 20% year‑1, require a 10% annual uplift on list pricing year‑3.

Monica — you have authority to finalize the term with the customer under these conditions and route the final doc to Legal + Finance for redline. Please confirm once the procurement team accepts.

- Vivek
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bloom <sara@greenlinehealth.com>, procurement@greenlinehealth.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final offer: Greenline Health renewal (DL-4721)

Hi Sara / Procurement — thanks for the patience. Following internal review, Redwood can do the following final package: 

- Annual renewal (12 months), annual billing
- Year‑1 discount: 18% off current list pricing
- One-time operational credit: $45,000 applied to the first invoice
- SLA: upgraded to 99.995% for the renewal term; we will provide an SLA playbook and quarterly incident reviews for the first year

If that works for Greenline, I'll send the formal contract and route to Legal/Finance for a fast-track sign. We'll also provide the DocuSign link and the final invoice schedule.

Next steps:
1) Please respond with approval by EOD Friday so we can hit Redwood's internal sign-off and Greenline's board timeline.
2) Once approved, I will share the DocuSign envelope and final proposal PDF.

Best,
Monica
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
